title: Stage 4 — API Architecture & HTTP
goal: Build a REST API with in-memory storage, structured JSON, middleware, and env config — verified with curl.
summary: HTTP, Express, REST, middleware pipeline, environment variables. The server exists before the UI connects.

checkpoint.prompt: Fetch the list of workouts without changing anything. Which method?
checkpoint.explanation: GET reads. POST creates. DELETE removes.

checkpoint.prompt: POST successfully creates a workout. Best status code?
checkpoint.explanation: 201 signals a new resource was created.

checkpoint.prompt: curl returns JSON but your browser UI fails later. Where is the bug likely first?

choices.text: Not in the API — curl proved the server works; debug the frontend in Stage 6
curl is always wrong; ignore it
The SQL database file is corrupt

checkpoint.explanation: curl isolates the API layer. If it works, the server side is solid.

checkpoint.prompt: You restart the API server. In-memory workouts disappear. Why?

choices.text: RAM is cleared — nothing was written to disk
Express deletes arrays on shutdown intentionally

checkpoint.explanation: In-memory storage is fine for learning; Stage 5 adds real persistence.

checkpoint.prompt: POST body fields are undefined in your handler. Most likely cause?

choices.text: `express.json()` middleware is missing or runs after the route
GET requests don't have bodies, so POST can't either

checkpoint.explanation: JSON body parsing is middleware — it must run before handlers that read req.body.

checklist.label: `api/` Express app runs on configurable PORT
Middleware: cors, json parser, request logger
POST validates input, returns 201 or 400 with envelope
GET and POST verified with curl

questions.prompt: What does the API layer do?

choices.text: Enforces rules and exposes data over HTTP

questions.explanation: The API sits between UI and storage — the contract clients call.

questions.prompt: Why test with curl before wiring the UI?

choices.text: Isolates the API layer so you know the server works first
curl is required for production deployment only

questions.explanation: curl removes browser, CORS, and JavaScript from debugging.
Without it, POST bodies are undefined.

questions.prompt: Why wrap success responses in `{ data: ... }`?

choices.text: Consistent shape so clients always know where to read the payload
JSON requires a data key by specification

questions.explanation: Structured envelopes keep frontend code predictable across endpoints.

questions.prompt: Why read `PORT` from `process.env` instead of hard-coding 3001?

choices.text: curl only works on env-configured ports

questions.explanation: Environment variables let the same code run locally and in deployment.
